column3: The Hebrew is verbless (“a wise son, a father’s discipline”); NASB adds “accepts.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He eats good things” is rendered “he enjoys good,” and “appetite” as “desire.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “comes to” (“comes to ruin”).
Close to the Hebrew; “His appetite” is rendered “The soul,” and NASB adds “gets.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A word of falsehood” is rendered “falsehood.”
“Righteousness preserves integrity of way … wickedness subverts sin” is rendered with persons, “the one whose way is blameless … the sinner.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Enriches himself … impoverishes himself” is rendered “pretends to be rich … pretends to be poor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A threat” is rendered “rebuke.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “Pride” is rendered “presumption,” and NASB adds “nothing but.”
“Wealth from vanity” is rendered “Wealth obtained by fraud,” and “gathers on hand” as “gathers by labor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A desire which comes” is rendered “desire fulfilled.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He will be pledged to it” is rendered “will be in debt to it.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Instruction” (torah) is rendered “teaching.”
“Enduring” is rendered “hard.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Spreads out” is rendered “displays.”
Close to the Hebrew; “An envoy of faithfulness” is rendered “a faithful envoy,” and NASB adds “brings.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “will come to him”; “correction” is rendered “reproof.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Pleasing to a person” is rendered “sweet to the soul.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “It rewards [with] good” is rendered “will be rewarded with prosperity.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“There is [what] is swept away in not justice” is rendered “it is swept away by injustice.” The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “Restrains his rod” is rendered “spares his rod,” and “seeks him early [with] discipline” as “disciplines him diligently.”
Close to the Hebrew.
